scope: Architecture-budget decision for promoting only the four blocker-closing Execution correctness candidates; host-restart report/permission continuity remains candidate-only.

remain_candidate_only.reason: Improves a safe waiting_user checkpoint but does not close the full recovery.host_restart_active_commission blocker because queued/working effect safety remains unresolved.
Improves safe permission-wait continuity but still does not close queued/working host-restart recovery and must not restore stale authorization state.

governance_decision.selected: Keep a base managed-patch budget of 10 and add at most four explicitly enumerated correctness-exception slots for blocker-closing groups.
governance_decision.why_not_plain_raise_to_16: Two host-restart candidates provide useful partial continuity but do not close their parent blocker; patch count must follow product correctness benefit, not candidate availability.
governance_decision.why_not_keep_hard_10: The four selected patches close five reproduced Execution blockers using existing N.E.K.O authorities and have full machine evidence; rejecting them solely because the arbitrary count reached ten would reduce product correctness without reducing duplicate-authority risk.
governance_decision.why_not_mega_patch: Combining logically separate candidates only to fit the old numeric cap would hide patch ownership and retirement boundaries.
governance_decision.why_not_external_workflow_engine: Would duplicate NekoClaw ledger/outbox/permission/runtime authority for gaps already expressible with native seams.

machine_policy_required: every exception patch is explicitly listed in a governance file
every exception belongs to a promotion group with one or more reproduced blocker ids
every group has existing machine acceptance and broad integration evidence
every exception has a formal patch reuse review and retirement condition
no candidate may be promoted merely because an exception slot is unused
host-restart report/permission candidates remain outside the live series
rollback: Remove the four exception patches from the managed series and restore core_patch_budget=10; no data migration or second authority is introduced.
retirement_condition: Reduce correctness-exception usage whenever upstream N.E.K.O absorbs equivalent behavior or an existing live patch becomes unnecessary; exception slots are not permanent entitlement.
